answer: HYPOTHESIS: Project Lead and Data Scientist are the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems — the source study reports 61.389% (95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) of respondents indicating association for Project Lead and 49.6% (95% CI [49.219, 49.981]) for Data Scientist. In the supplied 276-row dataset, the same two roles rank first and second by the share of respondents marking the role as addressing ML aspects in requirements (Q8_ML_Addressing_*): Project Lead 51.03% (99/194; respondent-level 95% bootstrap CI [43.81, 58.25]) and Data Scientist 48.97% (95/194; CI [41.75, 56.19]), clearly ahead of Business Analyst (25.77%), Developer (19.07%), Solution Architect (12.37%), Requirements Engineer (10.31%) and Tester (1.03%). Limitation: the source study's exact percentages and their very narrow CIs cannot be exactly reproduced from this file (no count fraction in the data equals 61.389%, and a ~0.4pp CI half-width implies an effective n far larger than the 194 valid respondents), so those figures are cited as the study's reported values; the reproduced estimates confirm the same top-2 roles and ordering.

payload.workflow: Loaded the 276-row survey CSV; encoded Q8_ML_Addressing_* as binary ('quoted'=1, 'not quoted'=0, '-77'=NA, the 82 suspended respondents who never reached the question; valid n=194); computed per-role proportions of association with requirements for the 7 named roles; resampled respondents with replacement 10,000 times (seed 42) and took percentile 95% CIs; ranked roles and identified the top two (Project Lead, Data Scientist); cross-checked the direction against the question's cited source-study figures (61.389% > 49.6%).
